svg.text: flat floes with a warm-white top and a slate edge in dark cold water; bergs
A. At fight distance, noon: the ground profile, the cover silhouettes, the far land as a value ladder. The two grey figures are 75 units tall (a fighter): scale only, no character art.
Palette at noon (the world-light tint per sky key multiplies it; lit, mid and shade are the three faces of one surface; the far ladder is each ridge hazed toward the horizon)

Readability (docs/art/dynamic-sky.md section 6): worst aura against any tone 20.7 CIEDE2000 (rule: 20 or more), worst Protagonist or rival body against ground, rock or vegetation 25.2 (rule: 15 or more), over every sky key with the world-light tint.
B. What the fight leaves: scorched (a beam along the ground), cratered (an impact), burned (fire on what grows)
a dark slate band across the floe, the water beside it steaming for a
the floe cracks in a star, the bowl floods with black water and the pieces
a soot-black floe and a lane of steaming water; cracked floes drifting
C. Destruction in sea ice: the impact at three moments (burst, peak, settle). A floe burst: white shards and chunks thrown out, black water ringing the cracks, a short column of white spray.
D. Where it meets its neighbours (hard steps in colour, never a fade; the cover mixes over about a third of the width)
The sea darkens to polar water and floe fragments appear, thickening into the
pack; the floe edges are slate.
Shore-fast ice: a flat white shelf along the coast, floes at its edge in dark
A shelf edge: a vertical slate cliff of ice over dark water, bergs calved off
